title: Synthetic journey probes for KV-cache effectiveness and SLI validation
creator: Marco Liu
description: Introduce an orchestrated synthetic probe system that runs lightweight, journey-style test traffic through the analytics ingest and console backend to validate SLIs and KV-cache behavior end-to-end. Probes will generate traceable requests that exercise common tenant journeys (ingest -> batching -> KV cache hit/miss -> aggregation -> dashboard ingestion) so we can detect regression in latency, error budgets, and cache effectiveness before customer impact.
background: We rely heavily on production telemetry and sampled traces to compute SLIs for analytics pipelines. This creates blind spots for regressions that only appear under specific request shapes (long prefix reuse leading to cache hotpaths, micro-bursts, or rare tooling flows). Existing SLI sampling strategies are optimized for cost, not exhaustive coverage. Synthetic probes can provide deterministic, continuous checks that link metrics, traces, and logs across the pipeline and validate alarm paths and runbooks end-to-end.
proposal: Build a scheduled probe orchestrator that: (1) replays a small corpus of seeded journeys derived from anonymized production traces, (2) tags each probe with deterministic trace IDs and tenant tags so traces can be correlated with metrics, (3) exercises KV cache hit and miss patterns, varying sequence lengths and burst patterns, (4) records probe metrics into the SLI evaluation pipeline (separate metric series with probe label) and (5) triggers synthetic-alerts when probe SLIs cross thresholds. The orchestrator should support adaptive scheduling to avoid biasing production metrics and a cost budget to cap probe token usage.
tasks: Design probe trace format and required headers/metadata for end-to-end correlation
Implement lightweight probe runner service (k8s job + concurrency limiter)
Create probe corpus generator that synthesizes journeys from anonymized traces
Add probe-labelled SLI metric streams and integrate with SLO evaluator
Extend tracing pipeline to preserve probe tags and full trace linkage through KV cache and batching components
Build dashboards to surface probe results side-by-side with production SLIs
Add adaptive scheduler that reduces probes during high load and backfills when safe
Write runbooks for synthetic-alerts and incident replay using probe traces
acceptance_criteria:
1) Probe service deploys to staging and can execute at least three distinct journeys that exercise KV cache hit path, miss path, and burst batching path.
2) Each probe generates a trace that links across ingest -> router -> runtime -> KV cache -> aggregator and is visible in tracing UI with the probe tag.
3) Probe-labelled SLI metrics appear in the SLO evaluator and are plotted in a dedicated dashboard.
4) An automated synthetic-alert fires when probe p99 latency > configured threshold and maps to the standard incident runbook.
5) Probe token usage is capped by a configurable budget and documented cost estimates are within 5% of projection.
6) No customer-facing dashboards or tenant metrics are polluted by synthetic probes (probe-level isolation verified).
risks: Probe traffic could skew cache statistics if not isolated or rate-limited
Anonymized trace-derived journeys may still leak tenant-identifiable patterns if sanitization is insufficient
Extra traces and metrics increase observability costs unless probe budgeted and sampled appropriately
False positives from synthetic-alerts due to probing during rolling deploys or transient infra upgrades
telemetry_contract: Probe metrics MUST include labels: probe_id, journey_type, tenant_shard, run_timestamp. Traces MUST include a probe.trace_id attribute and propagate through x-trace headers. Probe metrics are stored under metrics.probes.* and have a separate retention policy configurable per environment.
